```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

import calendar
import ocha_stratus as stratus
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from scipy.stats import spearmanr, linregress, mannwhitneyu
from statsmodels.othermod.betareg import BetaModel

# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
START_YEAR   = 1998   # first year used for trigger design
END_YEAR     = 2025
COLS         = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]
MOS          = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
N_ABOVE      = 3      # forecast arm: top N years per month
N_BELOW      = 5      # observation arm: bottom N years
FUTURE_YEARS = [2026, 2027]
TOTAL_YEARS  = END_YEAR - START_YEAR + 1   # 28

plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 120, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False})

def squeeze(y, n):
    """Map y ∈ (0,1) away from boundaries for beta regression."""
    return (y * (n - 1) + 0.5) / n

# ── Load data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
blob_name = (
    "ds-aa-ner-drought/raw/iri/ner_maproom_export_2026-04-25_thresh35 - Sheet1.csv"
)
df_raw = stratus.load_csv_from_blob(blob_name)
df_raw.columns = ["year", "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Aug", "JAS_SPI"]
df_raw["year"] = df_raw["year"].astype(int)
df_raw = df_raw.sort_values("year", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

month_cols = [c for c in df_raw.columns if c not in ("year", "Aug", "JAS_SPI")]
df_raw[month_cols] = df_raw[month_cols] / 100.0   # convert % → fraction

x_norm = df_raw["year"].values - df_raw["year"].values[0]   # 0 = most recent year
years  = df_raw["year"].values

keep       = df_raw["year"].values >= START_YEAR
x_norm_fit = x_norm[keep]
years_fit  = years[keep]
df_fit     = df_raw[df_raw["year"] >= START_YEAR].reset_index(drop=True)

# ── Beta regression (full historical record) ──────────────────────────────────
n_all = len(df_raw)
n_fit = len(df_fit)
X_all = np.column_stack([np.ones(n_all), x_norm])
X_fit = np.column_stack([np.ones(n_fit), x_norm_fit])

beta_results              = {}
df_detrended_beta_full    = df_raw[["year"]].copy()   # all years
df_detrended_beta         = df_fit[["year"]].copy()   # 1998+

beta_coef = {}  # col -> {coef, p, r2}
for col in COLS:
    res = BetaModel(squeeze(df_raw[col].values, n_all), X_all).fit(disp=False)
    beta_results[col] = res
    mean_trend = res.fittedvalues.mean()
    df_detrended_beta_full[col] = (df_raw[col].values / res.fittedvalues) * mean_trend
    df_detrended_beta[col]      = (df_fit[col].values / res.predict(X_fit)) * mean_trend
    beta_coef[col] = {
        "coef": round(res.params[1], 4),
        "p":    round(res.pvalues[1], 3),
        "r2":   round(float(np.corrcoef(res.fittedvalues,
                                        squeeze(df_raw[col].values, n_all))[0, 1] ** 2), 3),
    }

# ── Variance detrend (fit on full record, apply to 1998+) ─────────────────────
df_detrended_final = df_detrended_beta[["year"]].copy()
var_params = {}

for col in COLS:
    resid_all     = df_detrended_beta_full[col].values
    resid_mean    = resid_all.mean()
    abs_resid_all = np.abs(resid_all - resid_mean)
    abs_resid_mean = abs_resid_all.mean()
    slope_v, intercept_v, r_v, p_v, _ = linregress(x_norm, abs_resid_all)
    fitted_spread = np.clip(intercept_v + slope_v * x_norm_fit, 1e-3, None)
    resid_1998    = df_detrended_beta[col].values
    df_detrended_final[col] = (
        (resid_1998 - resid_mean) / fitted_spread
    ) * abs_resid_mean + resid_mean
    var_params[col] = {
        "resid_mean":    resid_mean,
        "abs_resid_mean": abs_resid_mean,
        "slope_v":       slope_v,
        "intercept_v":   intercept_v,
        "pvalue_v":      p_v,
        "r2_v":          r_v ** 2,
    }

# ── Merge with observation columns ────────────────────────────────────────────
df_stats = df_detrended_final.merge(df_raw[["year", "Aug", "JAS_SPI"]])

# ── Trigger design ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df_model = df_stats[df_stats["year"] >= START_YEAR].copy()
n = len(df_model)

for mo in MOS:
    col    = calendar.month_abbr[mo]
    thresh = df_model[col].nlargest(N_ABOVE).min() if N_ABOVE > 0 else np.inf
    df_model[f"trig_{col}"] = df_model[col] >= thresh

consec_cols = []
for second_mo in MOS[1:]:
    first_mo = second_mo - 1
    fc, sc   = calendar.month_abbr[first_mo], calendar.month_abbr[second_mo]
    df_model[f"trig_{fc}_{sc}"] = df_model[f"trig_{fc}"] & df_model[f"trig_{sc}"]
    consec_cols.append(f"trig_{fc}_{sc}")

df_model["trig_fcast"] = df_model[consec_cols].any(axis=1)
thresh_o = df_model["Aug"].nsmallest(N_BELOW).max() if N_BELOW > 0 else -np.inf
df_model["trig_obsv"]  = df_model["Aug"] <= thresh_o
df_model["trig_either"] = df_model["trig_fcast"] | df_model["trig_obsv"]

n_fcast_trig = int(df_model["trig_fcast"].sum())
n_obsv_trig  = int(df_model["trig_obsv"].sum())
n_trig       = int(df_model["trig_either"].sum())
rp_actual    = (n + 1) / n_trig

# ── Grid search over all (n_above, n_below) combinations ──────────────────────
_dicts = []
for _na in range(0, n + 1):
    for mo in MOS:
        col    = calendar.month_abbr[mo]
        thresh = df_model[col].nlargest(_na).min() if _na > 0 else np.inf
        df_model[f"_gs_{mo}"] = df_model[col] >= thresh
    _cc = []
    for _sm in MOS[1:]:
        _fm  = _sm - 1
        _c   = f"_gs_{_fm}_{_sm}"
        df_model[_c] = df_model[f"_gs_{_fm}"] & df_model[f"_gs_{_sm}"]
        _cc.append(_c)
    df_model["_gs_fcast"] = df_model[_cc].any(axis=1)
    _nf = int(df_model["_gs_fcast"].sum())
    for _nb in range(0, n + 1):
        _to = df_model["Aug"].nsmallest(_nb).max() if _nb > 0 else -np.inf
        _no = int((df_model["Aug"] <= _to).sum())
        _nt = int((df_model["_gs_fcast"] | (df_model["Aug"] <= _to)).sum())
        _dicts.append({"n_above": _na, "n_below": _nb, "n_fcast": _nf, "n_obsv": _no, "n_trig": _nt})
df_model.drop(columns=[c for c in df_model.columns if c.startswith("_gs_")], inplace=True)
df_qs = pd.DataFrame(_dicts).drop_duplicates(subset=["n_fcast", "n_obsv"])

# ── Back-transform thresholds ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
idx_asc   = np.argsort(years_fit)
years_asc = years_fit[idx_asc]
xnorm_asc = x_norm_fit[idx_asc]

year_start = df_raw["year"].values[0]   # 2025
thresh_py  = {}   # threshold per year, per month
trend_py       = {}
thresh_rows    = []

for mo in MOS:
    col  = calendar.month_abbr[mo]
    res  = beta_results[col]
    vp   = var_params[col]

    thresh_final = df_model[col].nlargest(N_ABOVE).min() if N_ABOVE > 0 else np.inf

    X_hist       = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(years_fit)), x_norm_fit])
    trend        = res.predict(X_hist)
    mean_trend   = res.fittedvalues.mean()

    fitted_spread = np.clip(vp["intercept_v"] + vp["slope_v"] * x_norm_fit, 1e-3, None)
    thresh_beta  = (
        (thresh_final - vp["resid_mean"]) * fitted_spread / vp["abs_resid_mean"]
        + vp["resid_mean"]
    )
    thresh_py[col] = thresh_beta * trend / mean_trend
    trend_py[col]  = trend

    future = {}
    for yr in FUTURE_YEARS:
        x_f       = yr - year_start
        trend_f   = float(res.predict(np.array([[1, x_f]]))[0])
        spread_f  = max(vp["intercept_v"] + vp["slope_v"] * x_f, 1e-3)
        beta_f    = (thresh_final - vp["resid_mean"]) * spread_f / vp["abs_resid_mean"] + vp["resid_mean"]
        future[yr] = round(beta_f * trend_f / mean_trend, 4)

    thresh_rows.append({
        "Month":              col,
        "Detrended thresh":   round(thresh_final, 4),
        **{str(yr): future[yr] for yr in FUTURE_YEARS},
    })

df_thresh_summary = pd.DataFrame(thresh_rows).set_index("Month")
```

## Overview

This document describes the design of an anticipatory action trigger for drought in Niger, based on IRI seasonal forecast probabilities and an August rainfall observation.

The trigger has **two independent arms** — either can fire to release early action:

- **Forecast arm**: fires when any two consecutive monthly IRI forecasts (January–June) are both in the top `{python} N_ABOVE` years per month in the detrended historical record. This results in **`{python} n_fcast_trig` total forecast-arm trigger years** out of `{python} TOTAL_YEARS`.
- **Observation arm**: fires when early August rainfall is among the bottom `{python} N_BELOW` driest years, covering **`{python} n_obsv_trig` observation-arm trigger years**.

The trigger is calibrated against `{python} TOTAL_YEARS` years of data (`{python} START_YEAR`–`{python} END_YEAR`), targeting approximately a **1-in-3.5 year** combined return period.

The forecast and observation arms are designed to each fire in **`{python} n_fcast_trig` years**, giving them equal probability of triggering. This represents a deliberate design choice: an earlier version of this framework used a much wider observation arm (proportionally far more observation-arm trigger years than forecast-arm years), meaning the trigger was far more likely to fire on the observation arm than the forecast arm. The revised design balances the two arms, preserving the value of the early warning signal from the forecast arm.

---

## Data

Three data sources are used:

| Variable | Description | Period |
|---|---|---|
| IRI Jan–Jun | Monthly probability of below-normal JAS precipitation (%) | 1991–2025 |
| Aug observation | August rainfall z-score (CHIRPS-based) | 1998–2025 |
| JAS SPI | July–August–September SPI (validation outcome) | 1998–2024 |

The IRI forecast probabilities are expressed as fractions (0–1) of the climatological below-normal tercile. The August observation is a standardised anomaly — lower (more negative) values indicate drier conditions.

The beta regression trend models are **fit on the full 1991–2025 record** to maximise sample size for estimating the long-term climate shift. The trigger threshold design uses **1998–2025 only**, matching the period of reliable operational data.

---

## Detrending

IRI seasonal forecast probabilities for below-normal precipitation show a declining trend over 1991–2025. This likely reflects the partial recovery of Sahelian rainfall since the 1970s–80s drought era, alongside improvements in the IRI model's baseline climatology. Without detrending, a historical percentile threshold would systematically favour recent years and underweight older drought signals.

We apply a two-step detrending procedure:

1. **Beta regression** — fits a trend curve bounded to (0, 1), appropriate for probability data. Divides out the trend so the series fluctuates around a constant mean.
2. **Variance standardisation** — fits a linear model to the absolute residuals over time, then rescales so the spread is constant across years.

The beta trend is fit on the **full historical record** (1991–2025); the variance model is also fit on all years. Both are then applied to the 1998–2025 analysis window.

### Detrending steps

```{python}
#| label: fig-detrend-steps
#| fig-cap: "Detrending pipeline for each forecast month. Blue = full-record beta trend; grey = raw observations. Col 1: mean-detrended series. Col 2: absolute residuals with linear spread fit. Col 3: fully detrended series."
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 18

idx   = np.argsort(years_fit)
yr_a  = years_fit[idx]
xn_a  = x_norm_fit[idx]
X_a   = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(yr_a)), xn_a])
df_r  = df_raw[df_raw["year"] >= START_YEAR].sort_values("year")

C_TREND = "#4477AA"
C_RAW   = "#AAAAAA"
C_VAR   = "#EE6677"

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(COLS), 4, figsize=(14, 18), sharex=True)

col_titles = ["Raw + beta trend", "Mean-detrended", "|Residual| spread", "Fully detrended"]
for j, t in enumerate(col_titles):
    axes[0, j].set_title(t, fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")

for i, col in enumerate(COLS):
    res  = beta_results[col]
    vp   = var_params[col]
    raw  = df_r[col].values
    mdet = df_detrended_beta.set_index("year").loc[yr_a, col].values
    fdet = df_detrended_final.set_index("year").loc[yr_a, col].values
    tr   = res.predict(X_a)
    absr = np.abs(mdet - vp["resid_mean"])
    spr  = np.clip(vp["intercept_v"] + vp["slope_v"] * xn_a, 1e-4, None)

    # Col 0
    ax = axes[i, 0]
    ax.scatter(yr_a, raw, s=14, color=C_RAW, alpha=0.85, zorder=3)
    ax.plot(yr_a, tr, color=C_TREND, lw=2,
            label=f"p={res.pvalues[1]:.3f}")
    ax.set_ylabel(col, fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right")

    # Col 1
    ax = axes[i, 1]
    ax.scatter(yr_a, mdet, s=14, color=C_TREND, alpha=0.8, zorder=3)
    ax.axhline(mdet.mean(), color=C_TREND, lw=1.2, ls="--")

    # Col 2
    ax = axes[i, 2]
    ax.scatter(yr_a, absr, s=14, color=C_TREND, alpha=0.8, zorder=3)
    ax.plot(yr_a, spr, color=C_VAR, lw=2,
            label=f"p={vp['pvalue_v']:.3f}")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right")

    # Col 3
    ax = axes[i, 3]
    ax.scatter(yr_a, fdet, s=14, color=C_TREND, alpha=0.8, zorder=3)
    ax.axhline(np.mean(fdet), color=C_TREND, lw=1.2, ls="--")

for j in range(4):
    axes[-1, j].set_xlabel("Year")

plt.suptitle(
    "Detrending steps — full historical record model (1991–2025)",
    fontsize=12, fontweight="bold",
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Model fit summary

```{python}
#| label: tbl-gof
#| tbl-cap: "Beta trend and variance fit quality. β R²: Pearson r² between fitted trend and squeezed observations. Var R²: r² of linear fit on |residual| vs year."

gof_rows = []
for col in COLS:
    gof_rows.append({
        "Month":  col,
        "β coef": beta_coef[col]["coef"],
        "β p":    beta_coef[col]["p"],
        "β R²":   beta_coef[col]["r2"],
        "Var R²": round(var_params[col]["r2_v"], 3),
        "Var p":  round(var_params[col]["pvalue_v"], 3),
    })

pd.DataFrame(gof_rows).set_index("Month").style.format({
    "β coef": "{:.4f}", "β p": "{:.3f}", "β R²": "{:.3f}",
    "Var R²": "{:.3f}", "Var p": "{:.3f}",
}).set_caption("")
```

A negative β coefficient indicates a declining trend in the below-normal forecast probability over time (fewer forecasts suggesting drought). The variance R² measures how much of the spread heteroscedasticity is explained by a linear trend in time.

### ROC AUC — lower-tercile drought years

The ROC AUC summarises how well each monthly forecast discriminates between drought years (JAS SPI below the lower tercile) and non-drought years. An AUC of 0.5 is no better than chance; 1.0 is perfect.

```{python}
#| label: fig-roc
#| fig-cap: "ROC AUC for each monthly IRI forecast against the binary outcome (JAS SPI below lower tercile). Values above 0.5 indicate useful forecast skill."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

def _auc(y_true, y_score):
    pos, neg = y_score[y_true == 1], y_score[y_true == 0]
    if len(pos) == 0 or len(neg) == 0:
        return 0.5
    u, _ = mannwhitneyu(pos, neg, alternative="greater")
    return float(u / (len(pos) * len(neg)))

_spi_vals = df_raw[df_raw["year"] >= START_YEAR]["JAS_SPI"].dropna().values
_tercile  = float(np.percentile(_spi_vals, 100 / 3))

_auc_raw, _auc_det = [], []
_sub_raw = df_raw[df_raw["year"] >= START_YEAR][COLS + ["JAS_SPI"]].dropna(subset=["JAS_SPI"])
_sub_det = df_stats[COLS + ["JAS_SPI"]].dropna(subset=["JAS_SPI"])
_yt      = (_sub_raw["JAS_SPI"].values < _tercile).astype(float)
_yt_det  = (_sub_det["JAS_SPI"].values < _tercile).astype(float)
for col in COLS:
    _auc_raw.append(_auc(_yt,     _sub_raw[col].values))
    _auc_det.append(_auc(_yt_det, _sub_det[col].values))

_x = np.arange(len(COLS))
_w = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.bar(_x - _w/2, _auc_raw, width=_w, label="Raw",      color="#4477AA", alpha=0.85)
ax.bar(_x + _w/2, _auc_det, width=_w, label="Detrended", color="#EE6677", alpha=0.85)
ax.axhline(0.5, color="gray", lw=1.2, ls="--", label="Random (0.5)")
ax.set_xticks(_x)
ax.set_xticklabels(COLS)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
ax.set_ylabel("AUC")
ax.set_title(f"ROC AUC vs JAS SPI < {_tercile:.2f} (lower tercile)")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Trigger Design

### Parameters

The trigger was designed over `{python} TOTAL_YEARS` years (`{python} START_YEAR`–`{python} END_YEAR`) using the **full historical record detrending model**. The selected thresholds fire in approximately `{python} n_trig` out of `{python} TOTAL_YEARS` years — a **1-in-`{python} round(rp_actual, 1)`** combined return period.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Analysis period | `{python} START_YEAR`–`{python} END_YEAR` (`{python} TOTAL_YEARS` years) |
| Detrending model | Full historical record (1991–2025) |
| Forecast arm: threshold per month | Top `{python} N_ABOVE` of `{python} TOTAL_YEARS` years per month |
| Forecast arm: total trigger years | `{python} n_fcast_trig` / `{python} TOTAL_YEARS` ≈ `{python} round(n_fcast_trig/TOTAL_YEARS*100, 1)`% |
| Observation arm: trigger years | Bottom `{python} N_BELOW` of `{python} TOTAL_YEARS` ≈ `{python} round(N_BELOW/TOTAL_YEARS*100, 1)`% |
| Total trigger years | `{python} n_trig` / `{python} TOTAL_YEARS` |
| Combined return period | ~1-in-`{python} round(rp_actual, 1)` years |

The **forecast arm** fires when any two *consecutive* monthly forecasts (e.g. Jan+Feb, Feb+Mar, …, May+Jun) are both in the top `{python} N_ABOVE` years for that month. Requiring consecutive months adds persistence, reducing false alarms from single-month spikes. Using top `{python} N_ABOVE` per month yields `{python} n_fcast_trig` total years in which the forecast arm fires — fewer than `{python} N_ABOVE` because not every year with one elevated month also has an elevated consecutive month.

The **observation arm** provides a safety net: it fires independently when the August rainfall observation is among the bottom `{python} N_BELOW` years, even if the forecast arm did not fire. Setting `{python} N_BELOW` = `{python} n_fcast_trig` gives both arms **equal trigger probability**, balancing the system so it is no more likely to release via observation than via forecast.

### Trigger arm comparison

The scatter below shows each historical year as a point. The x-axis is the August observation value (obs arm metric — lower is drier); the y-axis is the strongest consecutive forecast pair in that year, measured as the minimum of the two months' detrended values (forecast arm metric — higher means both months were elevated). Threshold lines mark where each arm fires. Points are coloured by which arm(s) triggered.

```{python}
#| label: fig-arm-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Each year plotted by its forecast-arm strength (y: max consecutive pair, min of the two months) vs its observation-arm value (x: Aug). Dashed lines mark the trigger thresholds. Colour shows which arm(s) fired."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6

_pairs = [(calendar.month_abbr[m-1], calendar.month_abbr[m]) for m in MOS[1:]]

_best_pair = []
for _, row in df_model.iterrows():
    _best_pair.append(max(min(row[a], row[b]) for a, b in _pairs))
_best_pair = np.array(_best_pair)

_aug_vals  = df_model["Aug"].values
_years_sc  = df_model["year"].values

_pair_thresh = max(
    min(df_model[a].nlargest(N_ABOVE).min(), df_model[b].nlargest(N_ABOVE).min())
    for a, b in _pairs
)

_COLORS = {
    "both":     "#9B2335",
    "forecast": "#4477AA",
    "obs":      "#EE6677",
    "neither":  "#BBBBBB",
}
_LABELS = {
    "both":     "Both arms",
    "forecast": "Forecast only",
    "obs":      "Obs only",
    "neither":  "Neither",
}

_cat = []
for i in range(len(df_model)):
    _f = bool(df_model["trig_fcast"].iloc[i])
    _o = bool(df_model["trig_obsv"].iloc[i])
    if _f and _o:
        _cat.append("both")
    elif _f:
        _cat.append("forecast")
    elif _o:
        _cat.append("obs")
    else:
        _cat.append("neither")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
for _k in ["both", "forecast", "obs", "neither"]:
    _m = [c == _k for c in _cat]
    ax.scatter(
        _aug_vals[_m], _best_pair[_m],
        color=_COLORS[_k], label=_LABELS[_k],
        s=60, alpha=0.9, edgecolors="white", linewidths=0.4, zorder=4,
    )

for i in range(len(df_model)):
    ax.annotate(
        str(_years_sc[i]),
        (_aug_vals[i], _best_pair[i]),
        fontsize=6.5, color="#333333",
        xytext=(3, 3), textcoords="offset points",
    )

ax.axvline(thresh_o, color="#EE6677", lw=1.5, ls="--", label=f"Obs threshold ({thresh_o:.2f})")
ax.axhline(_pair_thresh, color="#4477AA", lw=1.5, ls="--", label=f"Forecast threshold ({_pair_thresh:.2f})")
ax.set_xlabel("Aug observation (lower = drier)")
ax.set_ylabel("Best consecutive pair value\n(min of the two months, higher = stronger forecast)")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Back-Transformed Thresholds

The thresholds above are defined in **detrended space** — a stationary series where the declining trend has been removed. To apply the trigger in practice, we need the equivalent threshold in **raw forecast probability space** for each future year.

The back-transformation inverts both detrending steps using the fitted models, accounting for the expected beta trend and spread at each year. Because the underlying trend in below-normal probabilities is declining, the raw threshold for 2026–2027 is **lower** than it would have been in the 1990s — the trigger will fire at a lower absolute forecast probability, reflecting the changed climatology.

```{python}
#| label: fig-backtr
#| fig-cap: "Raw IRI forecast probabilities (grey) with beta trend (blue) and back-transformed trigger threshold (gold dashed). Red dots mark years that triggered in detrended space. Gold diamonds show the 2026 and 2027 threshold values."
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 8

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(14, 8))
_df_raw_fit = df_raw[df_raw["year"] >= START_YEAR].sort_values("year")

for i, mo in enumerate(MOS):
    col   = calendar.month_abbr[mo]
    ax    = axes[i // 3, i % 3]
    res   = beta_results[col]
    vp    = var_params[col]

    thresh_final = df_model[col].nlargest(N_ABOVE).min()
    trig_yrs     = set(df_model.loc[df_model[col] >= thresh_final, "year"].values)

    raw_vals  = _df_raw_fit[col].values
    trig_mask = np.array([y in trig_yrs for y in years_asc])
    trend_asc = trend_py[col][idx_asc]
    thr_asc   = thresh_py[col][idx_asc]

    ax.scatter(years_asc[~trig_mask], raw_vals[~trig_mask],
               s=18, color="#AAAAAA", alpha=0.8, label="raw data", zorder=3)
    ax.scatter(years_asc[trig_mask], raw_vals[trig_mask],
               s=55, color="#CC3311", alpha=0.9, zorder=5, label=f"triggered ({N_ABOVE})")
    ax.plot(years_asc, trend_asc,   color="#4477AA", lw=2,   label="beta trend")
    ax.plot(years_asc, thr_asc,     color="#CCBB44", lw=1.8, ls="--", label="threshold")

    for yr in FUTURE_YEARS:
        t_raw = df_thresh_summary.loc[col, str(yr)]
        ax.scatter(yr, t_raw, s=80, marker="D", color="#CCBB44", zorder=6)
        ax.annotate(f"{yr}: {t_raw:.3f}", (yr, t_raw),
                    xytext=(4, 6), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8)

    ax.set_title(col)
    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    if i == 0:
        ax.legend(fontsize=7)

for j in range(3):
    axes[1, j].set_xlabel("Year")

plt.suptitle(
    "Raw forecast probabilities + trend + back-transformed trigger threshold",
    fontsize=12, fontweight="bold",
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Forward-looking thresholds

The table below gives the trigger threshold in raw forecast probability space for 2026 and 2027. A monthly IRI below-normal probability **at or above** the value shown means that month contributes toward triggering the forecast arm (subject to the consecutive-month requirement).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-future
#| tbl-cap: "Back-transformed trigger thresholds for 2026 and 2027. Values are the minimum below-normal probability needed for a month to count toward the forecast arm trigger."

df_thresh_summary.style.format("{:.4f}").set_caption("")
```

These thresholds are lower than they would have been a decade ago, reflecting the declining climatological trend. The trigger is designed to remain calibrated to a consistent return period as the climate context evolves.
